justification: DQ-145 counted 5,274 served state-law (SEPP) rules with no citation verdict. scripts/state_law_proof.py tests each rule's whole text for a verbatim match in the instrument in force (legislation.nsw.gov.au HTML fetched once via the Fly app, sha256 in data/law_text_cache/manifest.json) and records the verdict and the clause it sits under. Read-only; scripts/apply_state_law_proof.py (not run) sets citation_status='proven' only for plan rows whose provision_text md5 is unchanged. No clause is written: the site reads none for state rows. RECOPY (follow-on, same branch): ~830 served state-law rows are the law's text stored imperfectly (ellipses, split sub-clauses, table/markdown leftovers, dash and ligature losses) and 49 are wording amended since. scripts/state_law_recopy.py cuts each cached instrument into its numbered units from the id paths the legislation HTML carries, picks the one smallest unit holding >=90% of a row's 5-word runs (several -> ambiguous, skipped), and accepts only if the unit text is verbatim by both provers, no content word of the row is missing from it, length ratio 0.8-3.0, no number vanishes; amended rows must be verbatim in the point-in-time law and absent today, same id path today. No model reads or writes text. scripts/apply_state_law_recopy.py (NOT run) writes the unit text with provision_versions history.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: a row whose text is not in the instrument is reported proven, or the candidate count differs from DQ-145's state-law share (5,274)
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Dry run 2026-10-16: 4,018 proven, 224 partial, 972 text_not_found of 5,214 mapped (60 unmapped non-SEPP rows listed); change-note fragments such as 'Specifies a minimum measurement (previously 3m, now 4.5m).' are text_not_found, as expected.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: the NSW legislation website's in-force text of each SEPP

real_layer_exempt.scripts/state_law_proof.py: read-only session (default_transaction_read_only=on); its real-layer check is its own dry run against production plus the cached legislation text (observed_red); a database-marked test would add nothing it does not already run

pre_impl.existing_data: 5,274 candidate rows across 9 SEPP titles x several document_id spellings; citation_status/citation_source_path/citation_checked_at exist (migrations 076-078)
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: assumed the HTML was cp1252; it is UTF-8. Assumed ref_number held clauses; most are 'provision_N'.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: reuses law_change_diff.paragraphs; dcp_citation_status.py is DCP/PDF-only and skips source_council IS NULL

functions.name: prove
functions.input: the stored provision_text of one served state-law rule row
functions.output: status proven/partial/text_not_found, tier, unique derived clause, clause candidates
functions.if_none: empty or heading-only text is text_not_found

functions.name: pick_unit
functions.input: one stored row text and an Instrument
functions.if_none: None with reason too_short / no_unit_holds_90pct / ambiguous

functions.name: judge
functions.output: ok flag, failed checks, words dropped, ratio, numbers lost
functions.if_none: empty unit text fails the verbatim check

values.value: 330 planned (302 partial, 28 amended) of 879; skips: 203 no unit holds 90%, 121 ambiguous, 70 length ratio, ~100 content word/number differs

break_it.scenario: a short sentence repeated in many clauses is 'proven' by any of them
break_it.what_happens: proof says the words exist, not which clause the rule came from
break_it.how: derived_clause is set only when every match sits under one clause; otherwise empty with candidates; 575 ambiguous rows

break_it.what_happens: a stale rule would be proven
break_it.how: whole-text match; the relaxed tier folds only whitespace, line-break hyphens and unicode dash/quote forms

break_it.scenario: row text changes between plan and apply
break_it.what_happens: a verdict would be written for text that was never proven
break_it.how: apply refuses on any md5 difference and verifies rowcount

break_it.scenario: the row is replaced by a unit that says something different (a stale or reworded rule)
break_it.what_happens: the served rule text silently changes its meaning
break_it.how: check b: every word of the row must be in the unit in order (only ellipsis, markers, markup, page furniture, lost f-ligatures and an end-of-row cut-off are explained); check d: no number may vanish

break_it.scenario: the same sentence appears in two clauses
break_it.what_happens: the wrong clause could be copied
break_it.how: more than one smallest qualifying unit is AMBIGUOUS and skipped (121 rows)

break_it.scenario: a number in the old text is not in the new
break_it.how: check d with thousands-group spellings folded

break_it.scenario: apply runs on rows that changed or already have version history
break_it.what_happens: history collides or newer text is overwritten
break_it.how: check_plan refuses md5 change, version rows, non-state rows, empty or U+FFFD text; one transaction, md5 and rowcount verified

mutation_analysis: Replacing Law.prove's match with 'return proven' fails test_changed_word_is_not_proven and test_garbled_text_not_found_and_empty. Recopy: replacing check d, check b, the ambiguity test or the ratio band with True each fail tests in tests/test_state_law_recopy.py (run 2026-10-17).
residual_risk: 31 proven rows are under 8 words (weak evidence). Proof is of text presence in the current instrument, not that the rule belongs to the stored clause. 'partial' (224) and 'text_not_found' (972) rows remain unproven and are DQ-88 candidates. APPLIED 2026-10-16: 4,001 + 70 rows proven live (backups state_law_proof_pre_*); 244 paraphrase rows withheld (v2_is_actionable=false, backup withhold_state_paraphrase_pre_*), user decision option 1 -- some are law fragments and come back once read. DQ-145 6,104 -> 1,796. Sol cross-review SKIPPED: diff over 512 KB (data files). RECOPY NOT APPLIED: 330 plan rows await --apply. 9 planned-looking rows hold version history and are skipped. A row that was a fragment (e.g. table cells) becomes its whole unit (ratio up to 3.0). state_law_proof2.prep now removes only an ASCII hyphen at a line break (it used to eat an em dash that ended a line, which made units ending 'must-' unprovable).
